observed_evidence.taiwan_central_bank: The Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) announced on September 17 that it kept the discount rate, secured-loan accommodation rate and short-term accommodation rate unchanged at 2.0%, 2.375% and 4.25%. It raised its 2026 real-GDP growth forecast to 11.48% and forecasts 5.82% for 2027. It forecasts 2026 headline CPI at 2.03% and core CPI at 2.16%, and 2027 headline/core CPI at 1.83%/1.89%. Effective September 18, the maximum LTV for a natural person's second home purchase rises from 60% to 70%, while no grace period remains.
observed_evidence.hormuz_shipping: Reuters reported preliminary ship-tracking data showing only three commercial vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, down from 12 the previous day and below the recent 10-day average of 17. Bab el-Mandeb crossings were also lower at 21 versus 24 the previous day. AIS-dark traffic means observed counts may understate actual movements.
observed_evidence.energy_market: Reuters reported Brent around $104.33/bbl and WTI around $101.34/bbl on September 17 as Saudi alternative loading via Oman eased crude-supply fears, while diesel markets remained exceptionally tight because of Middle East and Russian refinery disruptions.

semantic_interpretation: Taiwan monetary policy is less restrictive than a Fed-following hike scenario: the policy rate stays at 2%, while the central bank materially upgraded Taiwan growth and modestly eased selected housing-credit restrictions. This is supportive for domestic liquidity and rate-sensitive sectors, but the Fed's renewed tightening and energy inflation constrain the room for future easing. The collapse in observed Hormuz vessel traffic is a material escalation in physical shipping impairment despite Saudi mitigation via Oman; it keeps tail risks high for crude/LNG availability, freight, insurance and Taiwan's imported-energy costs.
